questions.question: What are the most common Ruby runtime errors?
questions.title: Common Ruby Runtime Errors
questions.direct_answer: The errors you'll see most: NoMethodError (calling a method that doesn't exist, often on nil — `nil.empty?` raises: undefined method empty? for nil); NameError (using an undefined variable/method: `foo` when foo isn't defined); ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments: `add(1,2,3)` for a 2-arg method); TypeError (wrong type: `"a" + 1` raises no implicit conversion of Integer into String); IndexError/KeyError (out-of-range array / missing hash key); ZeroDivisionError (n/0); RuntimeError (generic raise). The #1 cause: nil — a method returned nil when you expected an object, and you called a method on it. Fix: read the message (it names the method and receiver), check what returned nil (use &. or a default), and add a guard or a validation.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can name the common errors (NoMethodError on nil, ArgumentError count, TypeError) and that the #1 cause is nil.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Ignoring the error message (it names the method and receiver — read it), or not checking for nil before calling a method.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Common errors: NoMethodError (often nil), NameError, ArgumentError (count), TypeError, KeyError, ZeroDivisionError. #1 cause is nil — read the message; check what returned nil.

sections.title: Read the Message, Check for nil
sections.content: The errors you'll see most: NoMethodError (calling a method that doesn't exist, often on nil — nil dot empty raises undefined method empty for nil); NameError (using an undefined variable/method: foo when foo isn't defined); ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments: add 1 2 3 for a 2-arg method); TypeError (wrong type: a plus 1 raises no implicit conversion of Integer into String); IndexError or KeyError (out-of-range array / missing hash key); ZeroDivisionError (n divided by 0); RuntimeError (generic raise). The number one cause: nil — a method returned nil when you expected an object, and you called a method on it. Fix: read the message (it names the method and receiver), check what returned nil (use safe-navigation or a default), and add a guard or a validation.

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.content:
NoMethodError (often nil), NameError, ArgumentError (count), TypeError, KeyError, ZeroDivisionError. #1 cause: nil.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  N[NoMethodError] --> Nil[often nil.empty?]
  A[ArgumentError] --> C[wrong arg count]
  T[TypeError] --> W[wrong type]
  K[KeyError] --> M[missing hash key]
```

sections.title: Common runtime errors
sections.content:
```ruby
# NoMethodError: calling a method that doesn't exist (OFTEN on nil)
nil.empty?       # NoMethodError: undefined method `empty?' for nil
nil&.empty?      # nil (safe navigation: returns nil instead of raising)

# NameError: undefined variable/method
puts foo          # NameError: undefined local variable or method `foo'

# ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments
def add(a, b); a + b; end
add(1, 2, 3)     # ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 3, expected 2)

# TypeError: wrong type
'a' + 1          # TypeError: no implicit conversion of Integer into String
'a' + 1.to_s    # 'a1' (convert first)

# IndexError / KeyError
[1,2,3][10]      # nil (Array returns nil out of range; .fetch raises)
{a:1}.fetch(:b)  # KeyError: key not found (:b)

# ZeroDivisionError
1 / 0            # ZeroDivisionError: divided by 0

# The #1 cause is NIL: a method returned nil; you called a method on it.
# Fix: read the message (it names the method + receiver); guard with &. or a default.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Ignoring the error message — it names the method and the receiver (read it).
Not checking for nil before calling a method (use &. or a default).
Using [] on a hash that should raise on missing (use fetch for a KeyError).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: NoMethodError: method missing, most often on nil (nil.empty?).
NameError: undefined variable/method; ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments.
TypeError: wrong type ('a' + 1); KeyError: missing hash key (.fetch).
The #1 cause is nil — read the message (it names method+receiver); guard with &. or a default.

A common mistake is ignoring the error message, which names the method and receiver, and not checking for nil before calling a method.
